nba_directive.reason_text: This purchase client has a $5,227/mo payment at 6.5% and wants to revisit later — pinning a concrete callback with break-even math tied to today's achievable rate prevents the lead from going cold without pressuring them.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by anchoring their exact numbers to create urgency without pressure
  - State their current rate: 6.5% on a $571,343 balance at $5,227/mo
  - Pull today's best achievable rate for their profile and show the gap in real dollars (compute the new P&I at the achievable rate and present the monthly delta)
  - Example framing: 'At [achievable rate], your payment would be approximately $[computed figure] — that's $[delta] less every month you're in this home'

- Counter the 'wait for rates to drop' instinct with break-even math
  - Calculate closing costs for this purchase scenario and divide by the monthly savings to produce a break-even timeline in months
  - Remind them: if rates do drop later, they can refinance again — they are not locked in forever
  - Frame it as: 'Every month at 6.5% vs. [achievable rate] is a real cost; the break-even on locking now is only [X] months'

- Tie the delay to their stated life goal
  - Ask directly: 'What's the goal this home purchase is serving — retirement timeline, monthly cash flow, something else?'
  - Once they name it, reframe the rate gap as an obstacle to that goal: 'Each month at the higher rate is [monthly delta] not going toward [their goal]'

- Honor the delay but make it concrete — pin a callback, do not leave it open-ended
  - Propose a specific date and time: 'Let's put 15 minutes on the calendar for [specific day] — I'll have your full scenario ready so you can decide with real numbers in front of you'
  - Confirm via text reply so there is a written commitment
  - Set a personal reminder to follow up if no response within 48 hours — do not go silent after one attempt
